This pronoun, which is formed from the adverb ἐκεῖ [there], as Apollonius teaches in his work on adverbs p. 75, signifies a person or thing more remote, as οὗτος [this] signifies a person or thing nearer or present: about which it is said in the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 407. Its legitimate form is ἐκεῖνος [that one]: the disyllabic form the tragedians do not use except where the necessity of the meter demands; ἐκεῖνος [that one] is used either substantively or, less frequently, adjectivally.
There are few examples of the disyllabic forms.
